name: Motorcycle
description: Any motor vehicle with a seat or saddle on no more than three wheels; an electric two- or three-wheeler that is not an electric bicycle, moped or motorized scooter is a motorcycle, as is a seated electric scooter without pedals that can exceed 20 mph. Defined by Florida Statutes §316.003(47) and §320.01(26).

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground; includes autocycles but not mopeds or electric bicycles
An electric bike lands here once its motor exceeds 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W), it can exceed 30 mph, or it has no pedals and can exceed 20 mph
Florida has no separate electric motorcycle category

Riders need a motorcycle endorsement or a Motorcycle Only license, which requires passing the Basic RiderCourse; the licensing law defines the motorcycle needing one by engine displacement over 50 cc and doesn't say how an electric motor is measured
Riders and passengers must wear a helmet meeting FMVSS 218, except those over 21 covered by at least $10,000 in medical-benefits insurance
The operator must wear eye protection
Riders 16 or older needn't wear a helmet or eye protection on one rated at 2 brake horsepower or less that can't exceed 30 mph
Titled and registered with FLHSMV, with the plate permanently affixed and visible from the rear
Registering it doesn't require insurance: PIP and property damage liability proof applies only to vehicles with four or more wheels
Carries a passenger only on a seat designed for one
Not allowed on sidewalks or bicycle paths
